source: Grounded against the live src/ tree on 2026-05-01. Verify line ranges with the source-viewer button on each stage card; line numbers drift as code changes.

stages.title: Startup & Runtime Components
stages.tagline: Wire up Prompter, History, ActionManager, ObjectiveStack, MemoryBank, SelfPrompter, TranscriptLogger.
notes: initExamples runs in parallel via Promise.all (prompter.js ~line 112) which keeps startup snappy. Embedding-model init is implicit and not called out in the doc.
Spawn timeout is hardcoded to settings.spawn_timeout (~lines 120-125 of agent.js); if the bot fails to spawn, the agent exits gracefully.
Order matches the doc; no startup-time issues observed.

stages.title: Incoming Chat
stages.tagline: Filter, optionally translate, and route player messages to handleMessage().
notes: respondFunc handles both 'chat' and 'whisper'. Bot-self messages are ignored (~line 181) and configured chatter is filtered (~line 184).
Chat only triggers when serverProxy.getNumOtherAgents() === 0 (~line 216) — avoids multi-bot conflicts. NOT documented in bot-flow.md.
handleEnglishTranslation is called twice — once in _setupEventHandlers (~line 198) and again in handleMessage (~line 337). Likely redundant translation budget burn.

stages.title: Direct Command Shortcut
stages.tagline: If the player typed a valid !command, parse → validate → execute → return. No LLM call.
notes: Short-circuits before any model call. Validation, execution, response routing, then return.
!newAction is special-cased and DOES add the message to history before execution (~line 316). Undocumented exception to the 'no LLM for direct commands' rule.
Hardcoded regex in containsCommand (~line 29) means malformed commands fail silently rather than erroring.

stages.title: History Update
stages.tagline: Add the new turn to History (player→user, system→system, bot→assistant) and persist.
notes: OpenAI-style role mapping. Behavior logs from modes are inserted as system messages BEFORE the user request (~lines 348-356 of agent.js).
Mode behavior log is truncated at MAX_LOG=500 chars (~line 350). Worth checking when a behavior log was the missing context for a bad decision.
history.save() runs after every add — accumulates churn in high-frequency interactions.

stages.title: Prompt Preparation
stages.tagline: Fill the conversing template via replaceStrings: $NAME, $STATS, $INVENTORY, $COMMAND_DOCS, $EXAMPLES, $MEMORY, $CONVO, $LAST_GOALS, …
notes: $STATS aggregates stats + entities + nearbyBlocks (~lines 140-144). Three command calls per prompt — should be cached in self-prompt loops.
Example retrieval correctly uses latestIntentText() to focus on the most recent user request (the 'recent changes' note in the doc).
$BLUEPRINTS is filled even when no blueprints exist (yields empty string) — a candidate to drop conditionally to save tokens.

stages.title: LLM Request
stages.tagline: Send prepared prompt to the chat model. Cooldowns, retries (3x), staleness checks, sanitation.
notes: Cooldown (~line 219), 3 retries (~line 218), drops stale responses if a newer user message arrived (~lines 220-221, 273-281).
Strips </think> reasoning prefixes (~lines 283-286) and filters hallucinated '(FROM OTHER BOT)' mentions (~line 263).
Returns empty string on exhaustion — caller treats empty as 'stop the loop'.

stages.title: LLM Response Handling
stages.tagline: Empty → stop. Chat → reply. Command → truncate to first command, parse, validate, execute, re-prompt.
notes: truncCommandMessage drops everything after the first command (~line 382). The model often emits multi-step plans that get silently discarded.
Invalid commands add a system error to history and re-prompt (~lines 385-392).
max_responses comes from settings.max_commands or a caller override (~line 299).

stages.title: Command Execution
stages.tagline: Dispatch to commands/{actions,queries}.js, record transcript events, return result string.
notes: Strict argument validation: name, count, type, domain checks (~lines 126-170 of index.js).
Action and query commands share the same dispatcher; isAction() helper distinguishes them for mode logic (~line 184).
No automatic cap on command output size — each command is responsible for self-limiting. Easy place for a context-blowing surprise.

stages.title: Reasoning & Re-Prompt Loop
stages.tagline: After each command, append result as a system turn and prompt the model again. Capped by max_commands.
notes: The for loop at ~line 364 IS the reasoning loop. Three interrupt-injection points (~lines 346, 365, 395).
Self-prompt + user-message collision: max_responses is clamped to 1 to return control quickly (~lines 362-363).
No explicit reflection step — the model just gets the next system turn and infers what went wrong from raw output.

stages.title: Modes & Autonomous Follow-Up
stages.tagline: 300ms tick: update modes, run self-prompter, handle death/idle/disconnect events.
notes: 300ms tick (~line 575). flushBehaviorLog returns + clears the accumulated behavior text per tick.
Death event grabs the position into MemoryBank and triggers handleMessage with a death system prompt (~lines 537-559).
Self-prompt loop stops after MAX_NO_COMMAND=3 consecutive empty responses (~line 64).

stages.title: Memory System
stages.tagline: Three layers: recent History.turns, long-term History.memory summary, structured MemoryBank, plus TranscriptLogger for observability.
notes: When turns exceed settings.max_messages, an older chunk is removed and queued for summarization. The chunk is also archived to bots/{name}/histories/.
History.memory is hard-capped at 500 chars with the comment 'Compress it more next time' (~lines 55-57). This is where most long-horizon coherence is being lost.
MemoryBank is a flat key→value store; it grows unbounded across sessions if the bot keeps naming places.
TranscriptLogger covers chat/model/command/memory/lifecycle events — the foundation for any future eval harness.

stages.title: Why Tool Output Quality Matters
stages.tagline: Command output text becomes the next system turn — it directly steers the next decision.
notes: Each command emits its own free-text result; there is no shared response schema or error-code vocabulary.
No truncation at the dispatcher level — a 50KB chest dump could blow context if a command misbehaves.
ActionManager.getBotOutputSummary chops the MIDDLE of long outputs, which is exactly where the most informative tail messages tend to live.

stages.title: Multi-Model Layer / Prompter Internals
stages.tagline: Prompter routes promptConvo / promptCoding / promptMemSaving / promptVision to per-profile chat/code/vision/embedding models.
notes: _model_map.js auto-loads every adapter in src/models/ and infers the API from the model name prefix.
All adapters expose sendRequest(turns, systemMessage) and sendVisionRequest(...). New providers = new file with a static prefix.
Easy/cheap calls (memory summary, bot-responder, intent classify) currently use the same chat_model as the main reasoning step — clear cost win available.

doc_drift: Stage 2: chat only fires when getNumOtherAgents() === 0 — multi-bot avoidance is undocumented.
Stage 2: handleEnglishTranslation is called twice (event handler + handleMessage) — likely a redundant translation cost.
Stage 3: !newAction adds the message to history before executing, breaking the 'direct commands skip the LLM path' description.
Stage 5: latestIntentText() filtering rules are undocumented detail that affects example retrieval quality.
Stage 10: 300ms tick interval and the mode-update-then-self-prompter ordering aren't called out in the doc.
Stage 11: 500-char memory truncation is enforced in code but presented in the doc as just 'a short text summary' — that's the actual ceiling.
Stage 12: 'individual commands are responsible for conciseness' is the de-facto policy — there is no dispatcher-level cap.
Stage 13: Prompter also owns promptCoding and promptVision; the doc only highlights conversation prompting and memory-saving.
